text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
RussianOfficial(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
HoldCitizenship(x, y) ::: x holds citizenship y.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote can participate in the election.
CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegister(x) ::: If someone has US citizenship, then they can register to vote.
Citizenship(x) ∨ Citizenship(y) ::: A person either has US or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(vladimir, taiwan) ::: No Russian Federation official holds Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(vladimir, taiwan) ∧ ¬Manager(vladimir, gazprom) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(ekaterina) ∨ Manager(ekaterina, gazprom) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote or is a manager at Gazprom.
Conclusion:
¬(CanRegister(ekaterina) ∧ Participate(vladimir)) ::: It is not true that Ekaterina can register to vote and Vladimir can participate in the election.
